heroHeadline: Day 686: Peso Eases to ~17.05/USD as Sheinbaum Closes Tamaulipas Hospital Tour, Confirms Two Mexicans Died in Colombia Earthquake, and Reports Health-System Gains
heroSubtitle: August 18, 2026 marks Day 686 of Claudia Sheinbaum's presidency. Over the weekend she completed a Tamaulipas work tour, inaugurating a new 250-bed ISSSTE general hospital in Tampico (Aug 15) and a 179-bed IMSS-Bienestar hospital in Ciudad Madero (Aug 16) — her administration's 32nd hospital opening nationwide. On August 17 she confirmed two Mexican nationals died in Colombia's August 10 earthquake, with their remains repatriated and the embassy in Bogotá still searching for a missing couple in Pereira; Education Secretary Mario Delgado also announced 200,000+ new preparatoria spots and an August 24–25 national dialogue on classroom phone policy amid a broader push to regulate youth social-media use. On August 18, Sheinbaum reported specialist consultations up 60% since 2022 and 32 operating specialty hospitals, said a CDMX/Chiapas/Nuevo León gasoline shortage was resolved, and noted more than 1 million women had registered for the Pensión Mujeres Bienestar program since it opened August 1. She again dismissed U.S. scrutiny of Andy López Beltrán as political. The peso eased slightly to ~17.05 per dollar from the August 14 high of 16.98, still well above summer levels, as USMCA Round 4 talks remain set for Washington in early September with a separate Section 301 tariff determination looming as soon as August. Inflation held at 3.12% in July (lowest since May 2020), and approval sits at 57% (Aug 6 AtlasIntel) as Banxico's policy rate held at 6.50%.
